1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with ample letter spacing, line height, and padding inside white cards.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, no all-caps blocks, and only short paragraphs.

3.why: The single-column card layout with large tap targets and generous margins remains readable and uncluttered at mobile widths.

4.why: Every instruction is one or two plain-language sentences (e.g., 'Enter the six-digit identity code').

5.why: Recovery-code fields show a format example placeholder and OTP fields show '6 digits', but the identity-code field has no example of the expected input.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a brief sentence or two before the primary action is available.

7.why: The authenticator secret and recovery codes appear as selectable text that can be copied, although no one-click copy button is provided.

8.why: The setup flow mentions scanning a code but never displays a QR code or any equivalent visual alternative to manual secret entry.

9.why: Email and phone inputs are standard fields that browsers may autofill, yet one-time code fields give no evidence of password-manager or autocomplete support.

10.why: Page headings name the current step and the primary action is always a prominent full-width blue button.

11.why: Most screens present a single primary CTA, though the MFA settings and regenerate pages offer several co-equal actions at once.

12.why: Success states such as 'Authenticator verification succeeded' and 'Recovery code accepted' appear, yet they rarely state what the user should do next.

13.why: Users can retry via 'Start over', re-enter codes, or regenerate recovery codes with no lock-out or penalty shown.

14.why: The only error message observed ('The request could not be completed.') neither explains the problem nor tells the user how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers, session expiry warnings, or other time limits appear on any screen for reading or code entry.
